activities.name: One-Episode-a-Night via Apple TV App SharePlay
activities.one_liner: Start a FaceTime call, open the Apple TV app, and use native SharePlay to watch exactly one episode of a serialized show in sync every night, since both partners already have Apple accounts and don't need a matching third-party tool.
how_it_works: Start a 1:1 FaceTime call
Tap the SharePlay button, then open the Apple TV app from the SharePlay menu
Pick a show both have access to — Apple TV+ originals are the safest choice since Apple TV+ is confirmed live in Israel with Hebrew subtitle support
Press play; playback, pause, rewind, and fast-forward sync automatically for both participants
Cap it at one episode (roughly 22-55 min) and stop deliberately, preserving it as a nightly ritual rather than a binge
If a title is a rental/purchase rather than a subscription, each person needs their own access — SharePlay only syncs playback, it never grants content access to someone who doesn't already have it
tools_needed: Apple TV+ subscription or a purchased/rented title (per person)
activities.cost: free (if using an Apple TV+ subscription both already have) to paid (per-title rental/purchase)
activities.timezone_friction: Fits W1 (she's winding down, he's fresh) and W5 (he's fading, she's energized) because passive shared viewing tolerates both energy states; fits W7 because both are free. Apple TV+ being independently confirmed live in Israel with Hebrew subtitles removes the 'does she even have access' uncertainty that plagues Netflix/Prime for this specific app.

activities.name: Blind Rewatch with a Muted Opening Act
activities.one_liner: One partner picks a film or episode the other has never seen and keeps her own mic muted (camera optionally off) for the opening act over SharePlay, so his live reaction stays unprimed by hers, then both unmute to react together for the rest.
how_it_works: Start FaceTime, launch SharePlay in any app both can access (Apple TV app, Disney+, or Max all confirmed SharePlay-capable)
The picker chooses a title the other partner has genuinely never seen

During the opening act, the picker mutes her own FaceTime mic (and can turn her camera off) so her real-time reactions don't cue his — SharePlay keeps the video/audio playback synced regardless of each person's own mic/camera state
After the reveal or first act break, unmute and watch/react together normally for the remainder
Works with any SharePlay-capable app; the muting discipline is a manual practice layered on top of verified FaceTime controls, not a built-in feature of any streaming app
tools_needed: Any SharePlay-capable streaming app (Apple TV app / Disney+ / Max)
activities.timezone_friction: Needs both fully present and attentive to make the 'unprimed reaction' bit work, so it only fits W7 (both fresh, Saturday) or W6 if he's willing to pay the cost of staying up — the format is built around watching each other's face, which only works when both can actually look at the screen and each other.
activities.confidence_note: The underlying mechanics (independent mic/camera mute during a synced SharePlay session) are directly sourced from Apple's own documentation. The 'blind rewatch, muted reveal' ritual framing itself is my own construction built on those verified mechanics, not an independently documented named practice — flagged rather than presented as a cited ritual.

activities.name: One Short Episode Over Her Lunch via Disney+ or Max SharePlay
activities.one_liner: A single ~20-25 minute episode (animated series on Disney+, or a half-hour Max Original) watched in sync via SharePlay, sized to fit inside her 60-minute lunch break with a clean, pre-agreed stopping point.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call during her lunch window
Open Disney+ or Max (both confirmed to carry a SharePlay 'Supports' badge on their own App Store listings) and tap Share > SharePlay
Pick a single episode under 25 minutes — half-hour comedies and most animated series run short enough to finish inside the break
Watch synced; either partner can pause/control playback
Hard-stop at the episode's end — no 'one more episode,' since she has a fixed return-to-work time
tools_needed: Disney+ or Max app + subscription (both partners)
activities.cost: paid (Disney+ Israel: NIS 39.90/mo per Globes; Max Israel: NIS 49.90-64.90/mo per Jerusalem Post; US pricing not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: Chosen over Hulu deliberately: Hulu also carries a SharePlay badge but is a US-only service with no legitimate access path from Israel, which would make it unusable for him — a genuine region-lock finding, not an oversight. Disney+ and Max are both independently confirmed to operate in Israel, removing that blocker. Duration is kept at 25 min, safely inside W4's 60-minute hard cap.

activities.name: Max (HBO Max) Cross-Border SharePlay Co-Watch
activities.one_liner: Watch HBO/Max Originals in sync over FaceTime using Max's SharePlay feature — viable for this specific couple because Max's SharePlay went global for ad-free subscribers in 2024, and Max itself launched as a subscription service in Israel in January 2026.
how_it_works: Both partners need a Max subscription on one of the ad-free plans (SharePlay is restricted to ad-free tiers per Max's own rollout)
Start FaceTime, open the Max app, select something to watch
Tap Share, then SharePlay, and invite via the FaceTime call already in progress
Up to 32 people can join a session per Max's public documentation, though this is a two-person use case
Playback controls (pause, rewind, fast-forward) sync for both
activities.cost: paid (Israel: NIS 49.90-64.90/mo per Jerusalem Post launch coverage; US pricing not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: Confirmed technically cross-border capable (SharePlay itself works between an Israel-based and a US-based account) and Max is now a real subscription option in Israel as of Jan 2026 — but whether the ISRAELI Max catalog and the US Max catalog carry the SAME titles was not independently confirmed this session. This is flagged as an open question, not assumed.
activities.confidence_note: SharePlay-goes-global and Max-launches-in-Israel are each independently HIGH confidence from their own sources; the combination (do the two catalogs match) is unverified, so the activity as a whole is rated medium.

activities.name: Disney+ Native SharePlay Co-Watch
activities.one_liner: Watch a Disney+ film or series in sync via SharePlay — Disney+'s own App Store listing confirms native SharePlay support, and the service has been live in Israel since June 2022.
how_it_works: Both need a Disney+ subscription (available in both Israel and the US)
Start FaceTime, open Disney+, select a title, tap Share > SharePlay
Invite the other person through the active FaceTime call
Playback syncs automatically; either can pause/control

Note: Disney+'s older 'GroupWatch' feature, which required both viewers to be in the SAME country, was discontinued entirely on September 18, 2023 — SharePlay is the current and only cross-border option for this app
activities.cost: paid (Israel launch pricing: NIS 39.90/mo per Globes; US pricing not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: The discontinuation of GroupWatch (which explicitly blocked cross-country viewing) in favor of SharePlay (which does not carry that same-country restriction) is itself the key finding: this app went from region-locked-together to actually usable for an IL/US couple. Per-title catalog availability can still differ by region and was not checked title-by-title.

activities.name: Event-Grade Live Sports via SharePlay (the W6 Alarm-Worth-Setting Activity)
activities.one_liner: Watch a live sports broadcast or Twitch stream in real sync during W6 — her prime evening / his 1-5am — reserved for genuinely special events since it costs him real sleep, with an explicit pre-call rule against checking scores first.
how_it_works: Agree in advance on the specific game/event and confirm both have access (Apple TV app carries live sports like MLS and Friday Night Baseball per Apple's own documentation; Twitch is a free alternative for esports/other live streams)
Critical pre-call rule: he must not check any score, notification, or news app before the call, since he is 7 hours ahead and could otherwise see the result before she's even watching
Start FaceTime at the agreed W6 time, open the app, tap SharePlay
Watch live — there's no rewind/pause to manage since it's a live broadcast, just simultaneous viewing with synced audio
Reserve for genuinely special events (playoff games, a favorite team's big match), not a weekly habit, given the real cost to his sleep
tools_needed: Apple TV app (for MLS/Friday Night Baseball) or Twitch app (free)
activities.cost: free (Twitch) to paid (Apple TV channel subscriptions, MLS Season Pass, etc. — not independently priced this session)
activities.timezone_friction: This is the flagship W6 activity: it only works because he is willing to pay the cost of a 1-5am Israel viewing to catch her 6-10pm NYC evening live event. Explicitly not tagged to W1/W5 — those are passive, low-energy windows, and live sports demands real-time attention from both. The spoiler risk is uniquely severe here (unlike any recorded format in this thread) because of the asymmetric time gap.
activities.confidence_note: Apple TV app's own live-sports-via-SharePlay support (MLS, Friday Night Baseball) is HIGH confidence, directly sourced. An ESPN-specific SharePlay support article (support.espn.com) was referenced in search snippets but the page itself returned HTTP 403 on every direct fetch attempt this session and could not be independently verified — so ESPN-specific claims are excluded from how_it_works and the overall confidence is capped at medium.

activities.name: Netflix via Teleparty — No Native SharePlay, and a Real Region-Lock Wall
activities.one_liner: Netflix carries no native SharePlay support, so co-watching requires the Teleparty browser extension — and because Netflix explicitly requires household/extra members to be activated in the SAME country as the account owner, this couple cannot share one account across Israel/US and must each pay for and maintain their own regional subscription.
how_it_works: Confirm SharePlay is not an option: Netflix's own App Store listing carries no 'SharePlay' badge (checked directly), and Netflix's DRM blocks FaceTime screen-mirroring of its content too

Each partner needs their OWN Netflix account in their OWN country — Netflix's Help Center states outright that an extra household member 'must be activated in the same country where the account owner created it,' ruling out a shared IL/US household
Install the Teleparty browser extension (desktop/laptop only; actively maintained, with updates logged as recently as June-July 2026 per its own changelog) on both machines
Both start playback of the SAME title at the same moment via Teleparty's synced-play plus its text-chat sidebar

Verify the chosen title exists on BOTH the Israeli and the US Netflix catalog before committing — since each partner streams from their own region's library, a mismatch means one person simply can't watch it there
tools_needed: two separate Netflix subscriptions, one per region
FaceTime or a call for voice/video
activities.cost: paid (two separate Netflix subscriptions, priced in ILS and USD respectively)
activities.timezone_friction: This is the single biggest cross-border friction point found in the whole co-watching category. It does not fit W1/W3/W4 because Teleparty is desktop/browser-only — no phone-in-bed, no hands-busy commute use. It fits W5/W7, where both can sit at a laptop with time to verify catalog overlap first.

activities.name: Spotify Jam / SharePlay Group Listening Session
activities.one_liner: Start a FaceTime call, open Spotify, and pressing play automatically starts a Spotify Jam that syncs playback for both — Spotify's own support documentation confirms this works for participants in different locations, not just the same room.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call
The host opens Spotify and plays any song — Spotify Premium is required for the host, minimum, per Spotify's own SharePlay article
This auto-starts a Spotify Jam; the other person joins via the SharePlay prompt inside the FaceTime call
Both can control playback, skip tracks, and add to the shared queue

Important constraint straight from Spotify's own docs: 'If you started the session, leaving will end the session for everyone' — so whoever is more likely to need to duck out first should not be the host
activities.cost: paid (Spotify Premium for the host at minimum; exact price not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: Confirmed cross-country capable by Spotify's own documentation. The 'host leaving ends it for everyone' rule matters directly for this couple: her side of most windows has a hard stop (W4 lunch, W3 commute), so he should generally be the host to avoid an accidental mid-song shutdown when she has to go.

activities.name: Apple Music SharePlay Album Listen
activities.one_liner: Get on a FaceTime call and listen to a full album or playlist together via SharePlay — Apple's own documentation confirms only the HOST needs an Apple Music subscription, making this cheaper to run than Spotify's Jam if only one partner already pays for music.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call, tap SharePlay, choose the Music app

The host needs to be signed in and (per Apple's own guide) only the host needs an active Apple Music subscription — the other participant can listen along without paying, as long as they're signed into their Apple Account
Both can pause, skip, scrub, and add songs to the shared queue
Because it's audio-only once started, it can run in the background at a desk without demanding continuous screen attention
Works equally well as a short, bounded listen (one album side) or a longer ambient one
tools_needed: Apple Music subscription (host only, per Apple's own docs)
activities.cost: paid (one Apple Music subscription, host only)
activities.timezone_friction: Tagged for W4 specifically because once the Jam is running it's audio-only and doesn't force continuous screen-watching, which tolerates her being at a desk with a hard stop; the initial screen tap to start is brief and low-visibility. Also fits W1/W5 as low-effort ambient listening. Not tagged W3 because starting the session and browsing the queue does require occasional screen glances, which conflicts with a genuinely hands-busy commute.

activities.name: Audiobook Co-Listening via Download + Manual Countdown Sync
activities.one_liner: Both partners independently download the same audiobook chapter, open a voice call, and manually count down '3-2-1-play' to start together — the only verified audio-only, hands-free, screen-free format found anywhere in this thread, which makes it the answer to her commute.
how_it_works: Agree in advance on a book and the exact chapter/timestamp to start from

Each partner DOWNLOADS their own copy for offline playback rather than streaming live — this avoids a real Audible limitation where its Whispersync feature will jump playback position to whichever device is 'furthest ahead' if two people stream the same title live on one shared account
Start a phone call or FaceTime audio-only call (no video needed, which is exactly what her commute requires)
Count down together and press play at the same moment
Expect drift over a long chapter since there's no automatic sync; use natural pause points (chapter breaks) to re-sync verbally
tools_needed: Audible or Apple Books audiobooks (each partner owning/downloading the same title)
activities.cost: cheap (one audiobook credit/purchase; Amazon Household sharing can extend one Audible library to a second account at no extra cost per Amazon's own family-sharing feature)
activities.timezone_friction: This is the single best W3 format found in this entire research thread — no screen and no app-level sync needed once headphones are in, which tolerates her being mobile and hands-busy on transit completely. It also works for W1 since it's passive listening she can do half-asleep with the phone face-down.
activities.confidence_note: The Whispersync conflict and download workaround are confirmed by multiple independent secondary how-to sources, not by Audible's own official documentation addressing this exact two-listener scenario — downgraded from high accordingly.

activities.name: A Single YouTube Video Essay via FaceTime Screen Share
activities.one_liner: Since YouTube has no native SharePlay integration, watching a specific ~20-minute video essay or stand-up clip together requires old-fashioned FaceTime screen sharing — a workable but imperfect W4 option that requires her to actually look at a screen.
how_it_works: Pick a specific video in advance (a named video-essay channel's episode, not 'let's browse') so there's no dead time hunting for content on the call
Start FaceTime, tap the screen-share icon, open YouTube and play the video full-screen on the sharer's device
The other person watches the shared screen; audio comes through the call
Because YouTube is not a SharePlay app, only the sharer can pause/scrub — the viewer has no independent playback control, which matters if she has to stop abruptly to return to work
Expect noticeably lower video quality than a native SharePlay session, since screen-sharing re-encodes the video feed rather than syncing native playback
activities.timezone_friction: Included as the honest fallback for W4 short-form content, since YouTube — the best source of exactly-20-minute video essays and stand-up clips — has no native sync option. This is explicitly NOT hands-free or fully discreet: it requires looking at a screen and carries real audio, so it's a worse fit than the audio-only options in this thread for anyone in a genuinely public/silent-required space. Flagged as a real limitation rather than presented as a clean win.

activities.name: The Universal Fallback: Manual '3-2-1-Play' Sync
activities.one_liner: For any app with neither native SharePlay nor a Teleparty-style sync tool (a regional/local streaming app, a purchased DVD, a downloaded file), the fallback is a manually synchronized countdown over an open call — reliable for starting together, but it drifts over time and offers no shared pause/rewind.
how_it_works: Both cue up the exact same content to the exact same starting timestamp ahead of time
Keep a voice or video call open throughout, even though the media audio itself isn't tech-synced
Count down '3-2-1-play' together and press play at the same instant
Expect drift of several seconds to minutes over a long film; use natural breaks (chapter stops, 'let's pause here') to manually re-sync
If using FaceTime screen-sharing instead of two independent copies, expect a further quality drop, and be aware DRM-protected apps (Netflix confirmed) can black-screen when screen-shared
tools_needed: Any media source both own/subscribe to independently
activities.timezone_friction: The universal fallback, usable in any long-form window; deliberately not tagged to W3/W4 because it demands two full, independently cued copies in advance — not spontaneous enough for a hard-capped, mobile lunch or commute window.

activities.name: Syncplay for a Locally-Owned Video File
activities.one_liner: For a film neither streaming service carries in both countries (e.g., an Israeli production unavailable on any US platform), Syncplay is a free, open-source tool that synchronizes local video-player playback (VLC/mpv) across two independent computers.
how_it_works: Both partners need their own copy of the exact same video file
Install Syncplay (free) and a supported player (VLC or mpv) on both machines
Connect to the same Syncplay server room
Playback controls (play/pause/seek) sync automatically between both instances
Run a FaceTime audio call alongside for voice and reactions, since Syncplay itself has no video-call layer
tools_needed: a matching local video file, one copy per person
activities.timezone_friction: Niche but genuinely valuable specifically for content on neither shared streaming catalog — an Israeli show she can't get in the US, or vice versa, where one partner can legally send the other a file they already own. Desktop-only setup makes it a W5/W7 tool, not a thin-window one.
activities.confidence_note: Sourced only to a third-party 'alternatives' roundup found via WebSearch; Syncplay's own official site (syncplay.pl) was not independently opened this session. Confidence capped at low.

Free to use, each partner uses their own account; no country restriction found. Up to 32 viewers per SharePlay session per Twitch's original 2021 announcement.

Actively maintained as of July 2026 per its own public changelog (v5.7.3, supports 9 services including Netflix, Disney+, Max). Desktop/browser-only, no mobile app. Each partner still needs their own regional subscription and the title must exist in both catalogs.

No longer actively maintained as of 2026 per multiple third-party alternative-tool roundups; its own official status page was not independently opened this session.

Described as actively maintained and 'the gold standard' for local file sync by third-party roundups; Syncplay's own official site (syncplay.pl) was not independently opened this session, so this is lower-confidence than the App Store-verified entries above.

Operates entirely over iMessage, a mechanically different surface from FaceTime SharePlay. Recorded here only for the capability map, per the packet's instruction — this belongs to T3's territory, not T1's activity list.
No SharePlay badge on its App Store listing; correspondence/turn-based play doesn't need real-time SharePlay sync anyway. Recorded for the capability map only — belongs to T3.
A WebSearch snippet claimed SharePlay support, but the App Store listing fetch returned HTTP 404 this session and could not be independently verified.

thin_window_note: T1 served W4 with three entries (Disney+/Max short episode, YouTube video-essay screen-share, and Apple Music SharePlay tagged for lunch-desk listening) and W3 with one dedicated entry (audiobook manual-sync commute — the only audio-only, hands-free, screen-free format found anywhere in the co-watching/co-listening territory). That is 4 of 13 activities (~31%) touching W3/W4, clearing the shared preamble's 25% thin-window quota, with two of those (audiobook-commute and apple-music-lunch) meeting the stricter 'mobile/hands-busy or desk/public' sub-requirement. W6 was served by the live-sports entry and is usable via the long-form entries (Max, Disney+, blind rewatch) when picked deliberately as 'worth staying up for' — though W6 is not one of the five formally 'thin' windows defined by the shared preamble's cross-cutting quota (that set is W2/W3/W4/W8/W9), even though my brief separately named it as a window I own. T1 does NOT own and made no attempt to serve W2, W8, or W9 — per the thread map those belong to T2, T3, and T6; no entry in this file should be read as covering them.
gaps: Prime Video's SharePlay status is genuinely contested: some secondary blog sources claim support, but its own App Store listing (opened directly) shows no SharePlay badge, and Amazon quietly removed the older Watch Party feature around 2024. Recorded as unconfirmed/likely-unsupported in the appendix rather than guessed.

ESPN's SharePlay support could not be independently confirmed — support.espn.com's dedicated article returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt this session; only WebSearch snippet summaries were available, so it is marked 'unknown' in the appendix and excluded from the live-sports activity's sourced how_it_works.

Whether an Israeli Max account and a US Max account share the same title catalog (as opposed to both merely supporting the SharePlay mechanism) was not independently confirmed — flagged explicitly in that activity's timezone_friction as an open question for the couple to check themselves before relying on it.

Syncplay, Metastream, and Scener's current 2026 operating status came from third-party 'alternatives' roundup articles found via WebSearch, not each tool's own official site, which I did not independently open this session. Downgraded to low/medium confidence accordingly.

RiffTrax (a real, verifiable named audio-commentary product that would answer the must_cover 'commentary-track viewing' format) was investigated but its FAQ page returned 404 and its homepage did not confirm exact sync mechanics for a two-remote-viewer use case, so no activity entry was written for it rather than guessing at how it works.

'Reaction-cam viewing,' 'foreign-language film with subtitles,' and 'YouTube rabbit-hole night' (all named in the must_cover list as distinct formats) were not written as separate, independently-sourced activity entries. The first is effectively covered by SharePlay's inherent FaceTime video tiles (any SharePlay session already shows both faces live — see t1-apple-tv-app-nightly-episode's source). The second has no distinct verifiable 'format' beyond turning on subtitles, which felt too thin to justify its own sourced entry given the yield target. The third is a minor variant of t1-youtube-videoessay-screenshare without a meaningfully different mechanic or a new source. Quality/verifiability was prioritized over checking every named format box.

A specific Netflix per-country title-count comparison (found via WebSearch synthesis of thebestvpn.com, e.g. roughly 7,865 US titles) could not be verified because the source page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch. Excluded from the deliverable rather than cited unverified.

Zero reddit.com/r/LongDistance permalinks were obtained this session. Every WebFetch attempt to reddit.com and old.reddit.com was rejected by the tool itself ('unable to fetch'), and roughly eight WebSearch queries with varied phrasing targeting site:reddit.com/r/LongDistance returned no usable permalinks — this appears to be a tooling limitation rather than an absence of such threads. As a direct consequence, every entry in this file is sourced to official documentation, App Store listings, or identifiable tech press rather than first-person community accounts; confidence is generally higher as a result, but the 'real couples in their own words' texture the brief specifically asked for is entirely absent from T1.

Paramount+'s App Store listing fetch returned HTTP 404 this session; its SharePlay status (claimed by a WebSearch snippet but not independently opened) is marked 'unknown' in the appendix rather than assumed true.

COST SPREAD cross-cutting quota (majority should be free) was NOT met: roughly 6 of 13 activities are free (blind rewatch given an existing subscription, live-sports-via-Twitch, YouTube screen-share, the manual 3-2-1 fallback, Syncplay, and Apple TV app given an existing subscription); the remaining 7 require a paid streaming or music subscription by the nature of the named service. This looks like a structural property of the co-watching/co-listening territory rather than a research shortfall — nearly every named mainstream streaming and music service is inherently a paid product — and is reported honestly here per the quota's own instruction rather than forced to look compliant.

The web search budget for this multi-thread research session was exhausted partway through my final verification pass (shared across all six concurrent threads), which cut off a planned confirmation of RiffTrax's sync mechanics and Apple's official language on FaceTime video tiles during SharePlay. WebFetch remained available and was used for all remaining verification.
confidence_summary: MEDIUM-HIGH. Core SharePlay capability facts (which named apps support it) are HIGH confidence, verified directly via each app's own App Store 'Supports' badge and/or official support.apple.com, support.spotify.com, or vendor documentation opened directly this session. The region-lock findings are HIGH confidence for Netflix (official Netflix Help Center, opened directly) and for Disney+/Max/Apple TV+ availability in Israel (multiple reputable Israeli outlets: Globes, Jerusalem Post, Times of Israel, Haaretz). Weaker points, each flagged individually above and in the relevant activity's confidence_note, are: ESPN's SharePlay status, whether Max's IL and US catalogs actually match, and the current status of the third-party sync tools Syncplay/Metastream/Scener. Zero community-sourced (reddit) entries this session due to a tooling block on reddit.com/old.reddit.com fetches — noted as a limitation rather than papered over with invented permalinks.
